missed_issues: The two headline duplication numbers use inconsistent fork-treatment: §7.4 states the 10.1% exact-duplicate rate is fork-adjusted, but the 75.5% cross-org clone-pair share and the 702 exact clusters spanning >=2 orgs are computed on raw, non-fork-filtered pairs. So the cross-org clustering the abstract leans on is not fork-corrected and still counts fork-network copies as independent cross-org sharing. The review flagged the missing base rate; the raw-vs-adjusted inconsistency between the two headline figures is a separate issue.

The security-scan gate ('securityScan[n].status == clean') and the delegation receipts are, like the trace linkage, written by the orchestrator/agent into phase-state.json; the review marked only the traceability claim unsupported, but the same honor-system critique applies to the whole gate set, so 'cannot be bypassed via persuasive LLM prompting' is unsupported for the security-scan and delegation gates too, not just the trace. What runs the security scan and whether its 'clean' status is independently verifiable is never specified.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with the review's all-introduces/neutral pattern read (nothing is 'supports'; the system is unevaluated for effectiveness, conformance is tautological by the author's own admission, and the one comparator arm that could test the central thesis was run but withheld per Appendix D.4). The review is sharper than my blind pass in several correct ways: the headline duplicate rate is mis-denominated over ~30,581 tracked paths (~80% GitHub Actions workflows), the file-level CIs ignore clustering of 6,145 files within 846 repos (5,441 are .claude/** files), and 'hash-chained' overstates a per-line self-hash. My blind COI was low (candid design paper, employer's own tool, no comparative grading); I now agree the withheld comparator warrants the review's medium/2 (the merge raises it), which I verified against Appendix D.4. My reproducibility blind was 3 because the prevalence pipeline and dataset are released on Zenodo and runnable, though the Rel(AI)Build source and the comparator data are not; the review's 2 is defensible and the merge takes it.
